finding: Condition 5's two non-emptiness terms are unreachable given the same revision's §2.1 rule, so the section's normative claims about them are false. §2.1 now makes a round contribute no rows "when its stored `roles_hash` is empty or differs from the latest recorded round's", so an empty stored hash on the latest round makes that round contribute no rows, which by §2.2 gives `role_streaks: []` and by §2.3 gives `spec_coverage_clean_rounds: null`, which fails condition 1. Enumerate the cases: stored empty -> condition 1 already fails; stored non-empty and current empty -> plain equality already fails; on `--record` the two values are one stamped value, so the empty case is the first one again. Nothing is left for the non-emptiness terms to do. Yet §2.4 states "Both non-emptiness terms are load-bearing", and its later paragraph states of `--record` that "the non-emptiness terms are not [satisfied by construction], and they are what does the work there: a role file unreadable at record time stamps an empty hash and condition 5 fails" — it is condition 1 that withholds the object there, through §2.1's own new rule. Test 15, the only test of the terms, inherits the error: its fixture is exactly test 13's state (latest round's stored hash empty), where `spec_coverage_clean_rounds` is `null` and condition 1 fails, so its discriminating clause — "An implementation comparing the two strings without the non-emptiness terms emits the object under a panel it cannot name and fails" — cannot fail. This is the void-discriminating-clause defect the accepted finding on old test 40 named, reintroduced by the fix for the empty-hash findings.

finding: §2.1 closes the advisory rule with "on `--record` the round it names is necessarily an earlier one, since the round just stored always has a readable file". That justification only covers the three file-based causes. The fourth cause — an empty stored `roles_hash` — applies to the just-recorded round through a property of that round alone (§2.1 says so explicitly), and §2.1 itself states `ComputeRolesHash` returns an empty string with an error both audit callers discard, so an unreadable corpus at record time stamps `""` on the round being written. §2.4 and test 15 construct exactly that state on `--record`. In it the just-recorded round contributes no rows, and by §2.1's own rule ("a round in the walked segment that contributes no rows emits one advisory") the advisory fires naming the latest round — which the quoted sentence says cannot happen. Whether an advisory is emitted at all for a latest/just-recorded no-rows round, and which round number it names, is therefore unpinned: test 15 asserts only that `divergence` is absent, test 17 asserts only the empty array and the null, and test 10 assumes the earlier-round case. Two engineers write contradictory assertions (advisory present naming round N vs. no advisory).

finding: `role_streaks.consecutive_clean` carries a history only for roles that hold no open rows, and §2.2 itself concedes that "for a role holding open rows the streak is always 0 and says nothing `open` does not". The decision this release hands the operator is about the roles that DO hold open rows — are these findings chronic backlog or a regression the last repair introduced — and for exactly those roles the field is a constant 0. The justification offered for keeping the array under `--compact` ("a lens clean since round 2 and one that went clean this round after a repair both read `open: 0`, and only the streak separates them") describes roles that contribute nothing to `open_roles`/`other_roles_open` and therefore nothing to the operator's call, so the per-role bytes an agent parses on every `--status`/`--record` are spent on the half of the panel the decision does not turn on. Either the field's stated value is overclaimed or the earned half is missing.

finding: §2.4 says condition 5's two non-emptiness terms are "load-bearing", and test 15 claims an implementation that compares the two hashes without them "emits the object under a panel it cannot name and fails". Given §2.1's fourth no-rows cause that failure mode is unreachable, so neither term ever decides the outcome. Enumerate the states: (a) the latest round's stored hash is empty — §2.1 makes that round contribute no rows through a property of that round alone, so role_streaks is [] and spec_coverage_clean_rounds is null (test 13), and condition 1 already withholds divergence; (b) stored non-empty and the hash computed now empty — the two are then unequal, so the plain equality term already fails; (c) both empty — this is case (a). Test 15's fixture is case (c), so it passes against an implementation that keeps only the equality term. An implementer told a term is load-bearing writes it plus a guard test that cannot fail, and the recorded guarantee is weaker than the spec claims.

finding: §3.1 exempts `over-specification` from all three sinks — "the class stays in `mechanize_candidates`, never appears in `mechanized_classes`, and never joins the reviewer exclusion list" — but the reason it gives ("putting it on the do-not-report list would ship one prompt that both demands and forbids the same finding") only justifies the exclusion-list half. Applied to the candidate sink the exemption reproduces the exact defect §1 item 2 says this release fixes: with a valid `over-specification` entry registered, the class stays a candidate forever, so `len(candidates) > 0` stays true and the register-a-check `hint` ("write a mechanical check for each candidate class and register it") keeps telling the driver to write a check that already exists, every round, for the one class where re-registering it can never help. §3.2's "registration is the trigger" and §3.1's "registering a check is the operator asserting that it is" both point the other way for this sink.

finding: The revision replaced test 40's void `mechanical_checks` clause with the `skipping invalid check` notice as the observable, but the paragraph immediately above it — also new this revision — names the state where that notice is not emitted either. §3.2 now says "the runner needs a resolved task file to run in, so a check registered only in `.tp/config.json` for a spec that has no task file mechanizes its class while never executing"; `runMechanicalChecks` returns before its per-entry loop when the resolved task file path is empty, so no skip notice fires. The next paragraph nonetheless asserts "the sentence is absent from the prompt while the mechanical checks still run and each entry's skip notice is still emitted. That is the observable rule at both sites, and the skip notice is what makes it observable", and test 43 carries the same claim with no precondition ("the notice being the assertion that can fail"). In the boundary state §3.2 itself just named, both the dropped sentence and the absent notice are invisible, which is the unobservability the accepted finding on old test 40 was meant to close — narrowed rather than eliminated.

finding: §3.2's reviewer-exclusion paragraph says "Two changes to its membership, in this order and no others: entries the validator rejects are dropped, then the survivors collapse by class". That enumeration is closed ("and no others") but it omits a third change §3.1 requires: over-specification "never joins the reviewer exclusion list". Today the list is built from every registered entry's class (the panel site and the regression site both join all of wfChecks.Checks[i].Class), so removing over-specification is a real membership change, not a no-op. An implementer who builds §3.2 literally ships exactly the prompt §3.1 exists to prevent — one that both demands and forbids the over-specification class — and only test 36's exclusion-list half catches it. The fixture is therefore either redundant or specified with the wrong expected shape, and a tester writing it from §6 produces an assertion that contradicts test 13.
